lines.text: In 1983, one man stopped a nuclear war by refusing to believe a computer.

phrases.text: In 1983, one man stopped a nuclear war
by refusing to believe a computer.

lines.text: September twenty-sixth. A secret bunker near Moscow. Just after midnight. Three weeks earlier, the Soviets had shot down a passenger jet. Tension is at its peak.

phrases.text: September twenty-sixth. A secret bunker near Moscow.

lines.text: The alarm goes off: a US missile launch. Then another. Five in total. The computer rates it: high reliability.

phrases.text: The alarm goes off: a US missile launch.
Then another.
Five in total.

lines.text: Stanislav Petrov has minutes to report it. A report could trigger a counterstrike, and a full nuclear war.

phrases.text: Stanislav Petrov has minutes to report it.
A report could trigger a counterstrike,
and a full nuclear war.

lines.text: But a real attack would be hundreds of missiles, not five. And the ground radar/ sees nothing.

phrases.text: But a real attack would be hundreds of missiles, not five.

lines.text: He calls it a false alarm. And waits. Twenty-three minutes later, nothing has happened.

phrases.text: He calls it a false alarm.

lines.text: He was right. Sunlight on high clouds/ had fooled the satellites. The story stayed secret for fifteen years.

lines.text: Would you have trusted the computer? Tell me in the comments.
